bull.b: The sharp improvement from prior-year losses shows meaningful earnings recovery and product demand. Sustaining roughly 40% gross margins could support profitability as volumes normalize, although operating leverage still needs validation.

bull.t: Conservative current balance sheet and improved liquidity
bull.b: Low current leverage and stronger liquidity provide flexibility to fund product development and manage demand volatility. Reduced inventory also lowers working-capital risk, though historical capital-structure instability remains a constraint.

bull.t: Regulatory tailwinds and recurring software traction
bull.b: Restrictions on foreign or high-risk inverter suppliers may structurally improve demand for Tigo’s qualified domestic offerings. Growing Predict+ recurring revenue can add higher-visibility software income alongside hardware sales over time.

bear.t: Negative operating and free cash flow
bear.b: Recent accounting profitability has not converted into cash, indicating working-capital or operating pressures. Persistent negative free cash flow could require additional funding and limit investment capacity if the recovery stalls.

bear.t: Material revenue guidance reduction and delayed product ramps
bear.b: The guidance cut reflects delayed EG4 partner commercialization, slower GO Battery adoption, and a gradual European recovery. These issues reduce near-term revenue visibility and raise execution risk across key growth initiatives.

bear.t: Operating margin pressure and weak demand conditions
bear.b: Margin compression and near-breakeven adjusted EBITDA show that profitability remains fragile despite higher reported net income. U.S. residential weakness and softer European installations could prolong pressure on utilization and mix.
